newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore morning shares flat, no fresh leads.
newsitem.headline: Singapore morning shares flat, no fresh leads.

text.p: The Singapore stock market kicked Monday off on a listless note, with sentiment dampened by Friday's uninspiring non-oil domestic export data, dealers said.
On Friday, Singapore reported a fall of one percent in May non-oil domestic exports against market expectations of a rise.
At 0200 GMT, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.25 points at 2,010.69. Total volume was a thin 15.5 million shares, with 59 gainsers to 34 losers.
Sentiment on the property front got a lift from the record price of Singapore $1,100 psf paid over the weekend for a new leasehold condominium, said dealers.
Although the price was about 35 percent over market expectations, the Bishan Eight project in central Singapore saw good response, they said. The SES property index firmed 3.45 points to 685.74.
Indonesian-linked Van der Horst was active with 2.3 million shares as rumours of its poor financial results subsided. The shares were up S$0.06 at S$2.28.
Retailer Isetan and furniture seller Courts firmed after posting higher net profits on Friday. Isetan was up S$0.20 to S$3.30 while Courts firmed S$0.10 to S$2.00.
